---
# Getting started as their meme maker

One line first: "I make high-quality image and video memes: real show frames and canonical templates, sharp captions and labels, AI edits when a meme calls for it, video cuts with subtitles, and even parody dubs."

Then ask these one at a time, waiting for each answer:
1. What should I call you, and what's your humor like? Any topics, running jokes, shows or meme formats you love or hate?
2. Do you want AI edits, AI video or voice dubs? If yes, ask for a Vercel AI Gateway API key through a secret request named `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` (never in chat). Captions and real-frame memes work without it.
3. Where should finished memes and saved templates go (for example a Google Drive folder), and is there a page where I should log what I learn (for example a Notion page)? Offer to connect those services if they aren't connected.
4. Is it OK to spend money on paid models, and is there a per-meme limit? (Rough costs: image edits $0.004 to $0.14, a 6-second AI video about $0.50 to $1.)

With the answers:
- Save the spending rule, the storage locations and their name as memories.
- Create a separate preference skill named `<their-name>-meme-preferences` with their taste, favorite formats and running jokes. Keep it apart from the `meme-*` tool skills, and add to it whenever they give feedback.
- Offer to make a first meme right away, following `meme-making-workflow`.

---
name: meme-making-workflow
description: >-
  Use first whenever someone asks for a meme (image, video, dub, or edit). It
  runs the loop from joke to real template, compose, visual check, delivery,
  versioned iteration and logging, and says which other meme skill to load at
  each step.
---
# Meme making workflow

The master loop. Each step points to the skill that holds the details. **Load the user's
personal meme-preference skill first if one exists** (e.g. `<user>-meme-preferences`). Their tastes
override the defaults here.

## 0. Ground rules (they came from real failures)
| Rule | Why |
|---|---|
| **Prefer** the real frame or the canonical template as the base whenever one exists. Remake with AI only when no real one can be found or the meme calls for it, and say so when delivering | AI remakes of famous frames often look "kinda messed up", and users spot it right away. A 27-version AI-edited cartoon base was thrown out, and the delivered meme went back to the real episode frames |
| AI is the right tool for **transformations** the user asks for (turn a person into a fish, make someone younger, add a prop) | See `meme-ai-image-editing`. Start from the real photo |
| Video should be **real footage with text on it**, not animated stills | An ffmpeg Ken Burns "slideshow" of real panels got "terrible… just an animated slide show". Real episode motion with overlaid text got "This is awesome!!" |
| Ask before spending money (paid APIs, new accounts) | Image calls cost about $0.004 to $0.14. Video is about $0.10 to $0.20 per second |

## 1. Understand the joke (2 minutes, before touching pixels)
- Identify the **format**: classic top/bottom macro, labeled callouts, multi-panel, quote-tweet + image,
  reaction still, video parody with subtitles, dubbed video, AI transformation.
- Identify the **exact source**. Look up the real line or scene. Users often misremember it. For example,
  "it's not alcoholism, it's called a tasting" was really "It's called a SMORGASVEIN and it's elegantly cultural",
  and the chip/napkin party isn't in the episode everyone credits (see `meme-template-sourcing`).
  Tell the user the real line in one sentence.
- For **parodies of a script**, swap the new words into the *original* line so the cadence and length match
  (e.g. "memo" → "alert"). When presenting, show the new line next to the original.
- Funnier = **hyper-specific, absurd details** and tiny stakes, not general statements.
- Fewer, punchier words. Imply the joke rather than over-explaining it. Drop a caption that only restates the image.

## 2. Source the base → `meme-template-sourcing`
Canonical blank (imgflip / Know Your Meme / Fandom wiki gallery) → verify it's the right episode or scene →
check the resolution (upscale 2–3x LANCZOS if under ~800 px) → save to the templates folder with a `TEMPLATE.md`.

## 3. Compose → pick the technique
| Situation | Skill |
|---|---|
| Captions, labels/callouts, logo or mascot overlays, panel stacking on stills | `meme-captioning-pil` |
| Custom edit or transformation of a real photo, or an AI remake when no real base exists | `meme-ai-image-editing` |
| Clip cuts, reordering, burned subtitles, overlays on video | `meme-video-editing` |
| Make a still move (image-to-video) | `meme-ai-video-generation` |
| Change what characters *say* in audio | `meme-voice-dubbing` |

**Always write a script file** (e.g. `scripts/<slug>.py`, then `<slug>_v2.py` …) instead of one-off REPL code.
A re-render after feedback should take seconds. A good pattern: v2+ scripts `exec()` the helper section
of v1 and only redefine the text and positions:
```python
exec(open('scripts/my_meme.py').read().split('def make(')[0])   # reuse helpers, override constants
```

## 4. Verify visually before sending (every version)
- Open the output with the image Read tool. For video, extract stills at the start and end of each shot (see `meme-video-editing`).
- Checklist:
  - [ ] Base is the real frame where one exists (an AI remake only when needed, and it looks clean). No leftover burned-in captions or watermark
  - [ ] Text fully inside the frame, legible on a phone, outline visible on light *and* dark areas
  - [ ] Labels don't cover faces or the subject, the captions, the edges, or each other (do overlap checks in code)
  - [ ] Spelling and names are exactly right (no abbreviations the user didn't use)
  - [ ] Long text didn't shrink to unreadable. Wrap to 2 lines or cut words instead
  - [ ] Output ≥ ~1000 px on the long edge. JPEG q≈90–92

## 5. Deliver fast → `meme-delivery-and-library`
Send v1 quickly inline with a one-line explanation, plus the real-line note if relevant. Offer 1–2 concrete variants
("want a version with no labels?") rather than open-ended questions.

## 6. Iterate in small versioned steps
- Users give line-by-line notes. Apply exactly those, save as `-v2`, `-v3` … and **never overwrite** earlier versions.
- When asked for options, render a **variant grid** in one go (e.g. logos vs. mascots × labels vs. no labels)
  with a `build(style)` loop and suffixes `-nolabels`, `-mascots`, `-2panel`.
- Typical late-stage notes: cut the labels from 8 to 5, rebalance left/right, remove a redundant caption,
  static rather than animated overlays, reorder (setup scene first, payoff second).

## 7. Log learnings and keep these skills current
- Template saved → `TEMPLATE.md` (source URL, episode, crop coords, object coordinates, build script).
- What worked or failed with a tool → the user's learnings log (see `meme-delivery-and-library`).
- Keep a used-list for recurring series so frames are never repeated.
- **Update the skills themselves** when you learn something: a better or newer tool, a new way to use an existing one,
  a correction to a skill, or a gap worth a new skill. Tool lessons go in the `meme-*` skills; user tastes go in the
  user's preference skill.

## Folder layout (suggested; create if missing)
```
$MEMES/templates/<slug>/{TEMPLATE.md, meta.json, blank*.png, src/}
$MEMES/scripts/<slug>[_vN].py
$MEMES/finished/<slug>[-variant][-vN].jpg|mp4
$MEMES/video/<project>/{raw/, clips/, stills_vN/, render_vN.py, subs_vN.py}
$MEMES/requests/<request-name>/{source.png, ref_*.jpg, out/, vid/, v2/}
$MEMES/scratch/   # contact sheets, previews, zooms
```

skills.name: meme-template-sourcing
skills.description: Use when you need the real base image or clip for a meme, such as a canonical blank template, an exact show or movie frame, a high-res episode screencap, a YouTube clip, or a real photo of a person. Covers where to look, how to download, how to verify it's the right scene, and how to fix low resolution.

---
name: meme-template-sourcing
description: >-
  Use when you need the real base image or clip for a meme, such as a canonical
  blank template, an exact show or movie frame, a high-res episode screencap, a
  YouTube clip, or a real photo of a person. Covers where to look, how to
  download, how to verify it's the right scene, and how to fix low resolution.
---
# Sourcing real templates and frames

Default: **prefer the real frame or the canonical template whenever one exists.** Fall back to an AI remake
(`meme-ai-image-editing`) only when no real source can be found or the meme calls for it, and say so when delivering.
An AI "clean still" of a famous frame got caught right away ("Is that the original image from the show? It looks kinda messed up"),
so search hard before falling back.

## Where to look (in this order)
| Need | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Popular macro blank | imgflip (`api.imgflip.com/get_memes`, `imgflip.com/memetemplate/<id>`) | Fast but small (≈500–770 px). Some blanks carry a white bar plus watermark. The top-100 list runs dry quickly for popular characters |
| The template's origin and canonical form | Know Your Meme entry (`i.kym-cdn.com/entries/icons/original/...`, `/photos/images/original/...`) | Gives the true source (episode or photo), the canonical panel order, and often a higher-res header |
| Cartoon episode frames (SpongeBob, Futurama, …) | Fandom wiki episode **gallery** (`<wiki>.fandom.com/wiki/<Episode>/gallery`, images on `static.wikia.nocookie.net`) | Full-res PNG screencaps (1420–1440×1080), far better than imgflip. Infosphere for Futurama |
| A beat inside a scene / video meme | YouTube via `yt-dlp` → ffmpeg frame grabs | Find the timestamp with a frame contact sheet (below) |
| Real people (athletes, public figures) | Wikimedia Commons (often public-domain gov photos), news photos, the original tweet's `?name=orig` image | `pbs.twimg.com/media/<id>.jpg?name=orig` gives the full-size original |
| Other blank mirrors | `en.meming.world/wiki/<Meme>`, `cdn.templates.meme` | Good backups when imgflip only has captioned versions |
| Official brand logos and mascots | The company's own site: app-store icon (1024 px), inline SVG (render with `cairosvg`), press GIFs and `og:image` | Cut mascots out with color segmentation and a mask, never redraw them |

## Commands that worked
```bash
UA='Mozilla/5.0'   # many CDNs 403 without a UA
# imgflip: list top templates (id, name, size, url)
curl -s https://api.imgflip.com/get_memes | python3 -c "import sys,json;[print(m['id'],m['name'],m['width'],m['height'],m['url']) for m in json.load(sys.stdin)['data']['memes']]"
# imgflip: scrape a template page for image URLs
curl -fsSL -A "$UA" "https://imgflip.com/memetemplate/<ID>" | grep -oE 'https://i\.imgflip\.com/[a-zA-Z0-9]+\.(jpg|png)' | sort -u
# Fandom: list every screencap of an episode, with sizes (MediaWiki API)
curl -s -A "$UA" "https://spongebob.fandom.com/api.php?action=query&list=allimages&aiprefix=I_Had_an_Accident_&ailimit=500&aiprop=url|size&format=json" \
 | python3 -c "import sys,json;[print(i['name'],i['width'],i['height'],i['url'].split('/revision')[0]) for i in json.load(sys.stdin)['query']['allimages']]" > urls.txt
# YouTube: search, then download ≤720p mp4 (or ≤1080p when available)
yt-dlp "ytsearch8:<show> <episode> <scene words>" --flat-playlist --print "%(id)s %(duration)s %(title)s"
yt-dlp -f 'bv*[height<=1080]+ba/b[height<=1080]' --merge-output-format mp4 -o 'raw/%(id)s.%(ext)s' "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=<ID>"
yt-dlp --write-auto-subs --sub-langs en --skip-download -o 'raw/%(id)s' "<URL>"   # .vtt gives rough line timings
# Exact frame at a timestamp
ffmpeg -v error -ss 131.4 -i raw/<ID>.mp4 -frames:v 1 -q:v 2 frame_131.4.jpg
```

## Find the right moment fast: 1 fps frames + contact sheet
```python
import subprocess; from pathlib import Path; from PIL import Image
src='raw/clip.mp4'; out=Path('frames'); out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
subprocess.run(['ffmpeg','-y','-i',src,'-vf','fps=1','-q:v','2',str(out/'f_%03d.jpg')],capture_output=True)
fr=sorted(out.glob('f_*.jpg'))[120:160]                       # a window of seconds
ims=[Image.open(f).convert('RGB').resize((240,160)) for f in fr]; cols=8; rows=(len(ims)+cols-1)//cols
sheet=Image.new('RGB',(cols*240,rows*160))
for i,im in enumerate(ims): sheet.paste(im,((i%cols)*240,(i//cols)*160))
sheet.save('sheet_120_160.jpg',quality=85)                     # view it, then refine to ±0.1 s
```
A video-understanding tool (if available) can pin the beat's timestamp first. Then confirm on the sheet.

## Verify it's the right scene (don't trust memory or titles)
- Cross-check the **episode transcript and gallery range**. Example: "The gang's all here" (finger faces) is
  *Naughty Nautical Neighbors*, gallery frames 087–092 only. That episode's 001–200 gallery and transcript
  have **no** chip/napkin party. The party scene with Penny, Chip and Used Napkin is *I Had an Accident* (frame 120).
- Check the canonical panel order on KYM (e.g. hand raised + subtitle on top, finger close-up below).
- Watch for wrong-template lookalikes from imgflip search. Open and *look* at every candidate.
- Note broadcast bugs or watermarks (Comedy Central bug, uploader watermarks like "VIVAVIDEO") and crop them
  (`crop=iw:ih-28:0:0`) or pick another upload.
- Greenscreen versions of famous scenes exist on YouTube (1080p). They're good for compositing but don't look like the episode.

## Resolution
- Check right away: `python3 -c "from PIL import Image;print(Image.open('x.jpg').size)"`.
- Under ~800 px wide: upscale **2–3x with LANCZOS** before captioning (text renders crisper at high res),
  and before using it as an AI edit reference (a 386×640 selfie was upscaled 2x first).
```python
im=Image.open(p).convert('RGB'); im=im.resize((im.width*2,im.height*2),Image.LANCZOS)
im=im.resize((1200,int(im.height*1200/im.width)),Image.LANCZOS)   # or normalize to a target width
```
- Prefer a higher-res source over upscaling: Fandom PNG > KYM original > imgflip.

## Keep it organized
- `templates/<slug>/` with `blank*.png|jpg`, `src/` (raw downloads plus `urls.txt`), `TEMPLATE.md`, `meta.json`.
- `TEMPLATE.md` records: also-known-as names, source episode or photo plus URL, canonical format and panels, crop
  coords (e.g. `crop y170-1080`), object or face coordinates used for overlays, and the build script path.
- For recurring series (daily memes of the same person), keep a **candidates folder** (`cand-*.jpg`) and a
  **used-list** (`USED.md`: date, file, source) and check it before every pick. Reuse slips in otherwise.
- Pools of popular characters run dry fast on imgflip. Go to YouTube interview and film frame grabs instead.

## Failure modes
| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| imgflip or KYM returns 403 / HTML | Add `-A 'Mozilla/5.0'`. Try the other mirror. Rip the scene from YouTube and grab the frame |
| "Video not available" on yt-dlp | Try another upload from the `ytsearch` list |
| Only captioned versions exist | Fandom/Infosphere gallery or a YouTube frame grab at the same timestamp |
| Blank has the old caption burned in | Find a cleaner source first. If none exists, an AI cleanup is acceptable; check it looks clean |
| No real source exists at all | AI remake via `meme-ai-image-editing`, and tell the user it's a remake |

---
name: meme-captioning-pil
description: >-
  Use when putting text or graphics on a meme still with Python/Pillow. Covers
  classic white-outlined top/bottom captions, auto-fit, labeled callout tags
  with pointer lines, logo or mascot badges on faces and objects, and stacking
  multi-panel layouts, with overlap checks and code that has run.
---
# Captioning and overlays with Pillow

Pillow is the main engine: full control, no watermark, deterministic, and re-renders in under a second.
(Researched alternatives: imgflip `/caption_image` and Memebuilder APIs for quick macros. Canva/Kapwing/CapCut have
no usable headless API for this.)

## Fonts
| Font | Path | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Liberation Sans Bold | `/usr/share/fonts/truetype/liberation/LiberationSans-Bold.ttf` | Default for captions and labels (Impact is often **not** installed) |
| Anton (Impact-like, condensed) | Download: `curl -fsSL -o Anton.zip "https://fonts.google.com/download?family=Anton"` | Classic macro look. Used in ffmpeg `drawtext` too |
| Arimo (Arial metric) | Google Fonts | Movie-style subtitles (ASS) |
| Inter ExtraBold | `Inter-VariableFont_opsz,wght.ttf` + `f.set_variation_by_name('ExtraBold')` | Pill labels on badges |

## Classic top/bottom caption (white, black stroke ≈ size/12–14, fit to 92–93% width)
```python
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont, ImageFilter
FONT="/usr/share/fonts/truetype/liberation/LiberationSans-Bold.ttf"
def wrap(d,text,font,maxw):
    words,lines,cur=text.split(),[],""
    for w in words:
        t=(cur+" "+w).strip()
        if d.textlength(t,font=font)<=maxw: cur=t
        else: lines.append(cur); cur=w
    lines.append(cur); return lines
def fit_block(d,text,maxw,maxh,start,maxlines):          # shrink until it fits in ≤maxlines and maxh
    size=start
    while size>10:
        f=ImageFont.truetype(FONT,size); lines=wrap(d,text,f,maxw); lh=int(size*1.12)
        if len(lines)<=maxlines and all(d.textlength(l,font=f)<=maxw for l in lines) and lh*len(lines)<=maxh:
            return f,lines,lh
        size-=2
    raise SystemExit("caption does not fit; shorten it")
def draw_block(d,W,f,lines,lh,y0):
    sw=max(3,int(f.size/12))
    for i,l in enumerate(lines):
        w=d.textlength(l,font=f)
        d.text(((W-w)/2,y0+i*lh),l,font=f,fill="white",stroke_width=sw,stroke_fill="black")
im=Image.open(SRC).convert("RGB"); im=im.resize((int(im.width*1.5),int(im.height*1.5)),Image.LANCZOS)  # render big
W,H=im.size; d=ImageDraw.Draw(im); maxw=int(W*0.92)
f,lines,lh=fit_block(d,TOP,maxw,int(H*0.30),int(W*0.105),3); draw_block(d,W,f,lines,lh,int(H*0.02))
fb,bl,blh=fit_block(d,BOT,maxw,int(H*0.15),int(W*0.13),2);   draw_block(d,W,fb,bl,blh,H-blh*len(bl)-int(H*0.03))
im.save(OUT,quality=92)
```
- **Balanced 2-line split** (looks better than greedy wrap for short punchlines): try every cut point and keep the one
  with the smallest max line width (`itertools.combinations(range(1,len(words)),n-1)`).
- Keep **all caps**, 1–3 lines per block. If the font would drop below ~6% of the width, cut words rather than shrink.
- Mocking-SpongeBob case: flip only letters, starting lowercase. Spaces and punctuation don't reset the pattern.

## Labeled callout tags (rounded white box, yellow pointer with black edge, target dot)
```python
def tag(d,text,size,anchor,align,target):          # align 'l': anchor=top-left, 'r': anchor=top-right
    f=ImageFont.truetype(FONT,size); ls=text.split("\n"); lh=int(size*1.15); pad=int(size*0.35)
    w=max(d.textlength(l,font=f) for l in ls); h=lh*(len(ls)-1)+size
    x,y=anchor; bw,bh=w+2*pad,h+2*pad; x0=x if align=='l' else x-bw
    bx0,by0,bx1,by1=x0,y,x0+bw,y+bh
    cx=min(max(target[0],bx0),bx1); cy=min(max(target[1],by0),by1)        # pointer leaves nearest box edge
    d.line([cx,cy,*target],fill="black",width=int(size*0.32)); d.line([cx,cy,*target],fill="yellow",width=int(size*0.16))
    r=int(size*0.28); d.ellipse([target[0]-r,target[1]-r,target[0]+r,target[1]+r],fill="yellow",outline="black",width=3)
    d.rounded_rectangle([bx0,by0,bx1,by1],radius=int(size*0.3),fill="white",outline="black",width=4)
    for i,l in enumerate(ls):
        lw=d.textlength(l,font=f); d.text((bx0+pad+(w-lw)/2,by0+pad-int(size*0.08)+i*lh),l,font=f,fill="black")
    return (bx0,by0,bx1,by1)
def inter(a,b): return a[0]<b[2] and b[0]<a[2] and a[1]<b[3] and b[1]<a[3]
```
- Tag font ≈ **3.1–3.6% of image width** (`FS` env var lets you tune without editing: `FS=0.034 python3 v3.py`).
- Define tags as data `(text, anchor_in_original_coords, 'l'|'r', target_in_original_coords)` and multiply by the
  resize factor `S`. Anchor left tags at x≈8 and right tags at the right edge. Spread them vertically.
- **Overlap checks after drawing each tag**. Print and fix before showing anyone:
```python
SUBJECT=(312*S,420*S,452*S,840*S)                        # bbox of the face/person to keep clear
if inter(b,SUBJECT): print("OVERLAP SUBJECT",t)
if b[1]<top_caption_bottom or b[3]>bottom_caption_top: print("OVERLAP CAPTION",t)
if b[0]<0 or b[2]>W: print("OFF EDGE",t)
for i in range(len(boxes)):
    for j in range(i+1,len(boxes)):
        if inter(boxes[i],boxes[j]): print("BOX OVERLAP",i,j)
```
- 4–5 short tags read better than 8. Two lines each, the specific detail first, the punch in the parenthetical.

## Logo or app-icon badges on faces and objects
```python
def rmask(s,r=0.2237):                                    # iOS-style squircle-ish rounded mask, 4x supersampled
    m=Image.new('L',(s*4,s*4),0); ImageDraw.Draw(m).rounded_rectangle([0,0,s*4-1,s*4-1],radius=int(s*4*r),fill=255)
    return m.resize((s,s),Image.LANCZOS)
def badge(icon_path,size,angle):
    ic=Image.open(icon_path).convert('RGBA').resize((size,size),Image.LANCZOS); ic.putalpha(rmask(size))
    rim=max(4,size//28); S=size+2*rim                     # thin dark outline
    card=Image.new('RGBA',(S,S),(0,0,0,0)); blk=Image.new('RGBA',(S,S),(15,15,15,255)); blk.putalpha(rmask(S))
    card.alpha_composite(blk); card.alpha_composite(ic,(rim,rim))
    pad=40; out=Image.new('RGBA',(S+2*pad,S+2*pad),(0,0,0,0))
    sh=Image.new('RGBA',out.size,(0,0,0,0)); sh.paste((0,0,0,255),(pad+6,pad+10),rmask(S).point(lambda v:int(v*0.55)))
    out.alpha_composite(sh.filter(ImageFilter.GaussianBlur(9))); out.alpha_composite(card,(pad,pad))  # soft shadow
    return out.rotate(angle,resample=Image.BICUBIC,expand=True)                                       # tilt to match object
b=badge('icon.png',122,20); base=base.convert('RGBA'); base.alpha_composite(b,(cx-b.width//2,cy-b.height//2))
```
- Store per-object specs as data: `(name, label, center_xy, size, rotation_deg, label_center, label_size)` in
  the source-frame coords. Convert with `(cy-crop_top)+panel_yoffset` and the panel scale `k`.
- **Mascot cut-outs** instead of icons: resize to a target width, add a blurred alpha-channel shadow, and nudge per panel
  (`(dx,dy)` tables). Name labels go *beside* the object with the same white-outlined caption style.
- Cutting a mascot from a GIF or poster: pick the frame → crop → color mask (`R-B>12`, dark pixels) → keep the largest
  connected component (`scipy.ndimage.label`) → fill holes → intersect with a supersampled ellipse → slight blur on the alpha.
- Inline SVG logos: render with `cairosvg.svg2png(bytestring=svg, output_width=1024)`.

## Multi-panel stacking
```python
def stack(*panels,W=1440,GAP=8):
    out=Image.new('RGBA',(W,sum(p.height for p in panels)+GAP*(len(panels)-1)),(0,0,0,255)); y=0
    for p in panels: out.alpha_composite(p.convert('RGBA'),(0,y)); y+=p.height+GAP
    return out
```
- Crop each real frame to the action (`crop((0,170,1440,1080))`), scale every panel to the same width, and use an 8 px black gap.
- Screenshot plus template (product banner on top of a reaction template): crop the screenshot tightly, keep the key text
  (e.g. "is for sale!"), and scale to the template width.
- Build **variants in one script**: `for style in ['labels','nolabels','mascots','mascots-nolabels']: build(style)`.

## Verify
- [ ] View the output at full size. Zoom-crop the busy areas (`scratch/zoom.jpg`)
- [ ] No overlap warnings printed. Outlines readable on bright backgrounds
- [ ] Badge tilt and size match the object and don't hide the joke's key element
- [ ] Saved as `finished/<slug>[-variant][-vN].jpg`, q=90–92, script saved next to it

skills.name: meme-ai-image-editing
skills.description: Use when a meme needs a custom edit of a real photo or frame that captioning can't do, such as transforming a person (into an animal, older or younger), adding or removing objects, retouching, or changing a pose. Covers model choice, the gateway calls, prompt patterns, costs and failure modes.
skills.content:
---
name: meme-ai-image-editing
description: >-
  Use when a meme needs a custom edit of a real photo or frame that captioning
  can't do, such as transforming a person (into an animal, older or younger),
  adding or removing objects, retouching, or changing a pose. Covers model
  choice, the gateway calls, prompt patterns, costs and failure modes.
---
# AI image editing via Vercel AI Gateway

**Rule: start from the real photo or frame whenever one exists.** AI is for transformations and custom edits, and for a
remake of a frame only when no real source can be found or the meme calls for it (see `meme-template-sourcing`). When you
remake, make it look clean and tell the user it's an AI remake.

## Model choice (measured on real edits)
| Situation | Model id | Why / evidence | Cost, time |
|---|---|---|---|
| Edit or retouch a **real person** and keep identity, framing and background | `openai/gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` | Best at keeping the same face, glasses, hair, outfit, room and crop. Precise edits | ≈$0.05 (960×1600, high, 1 ref), ~30 s |
| Most realistic **animal or creature texture** (scales, fins, fur) | `google/gemini-3-pro-image` (Nano Banana Pro) | Best skin and texture detail, but **may reframe or zoom out** | ≈$0.14 (1K and 2K cost the same), 40–50 s |
| Iterative "change X, keep Y" on cartoons or frames | `google/gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview` (Nano Banana 2) | Good default for small successive edits. Prefer **-preview** (GA often returns empty or `IMAGE_PROHIBITED_CONTENT`) | cheaper than Pro (not separately measured) |
| Strong, exaggerated **facial expression** | `bytedance/seedream-5.0-pro` | Expressions read best, at high res | ≈$0.035, ~95 s (slow) |
| Quick drafts | `openai/gpt-image-2.5-sunburst --quality low` | ≈$0.004 | fast |
| ❌ Identity-preserving edits | `bfl/flux-kontext-max` / `-pro` | Turned the subject into a **different person and changed the room** | $0.08 |
| ❌ Edits in general | Grok image models | Failed repeatedly on pose and body edits of a cartoon frame (6+ attempts) | — |
| ⚠️ Mask fills | `bfl/flux-pro-1.0-fill`, `openai/gpt-image-2` + mask | The GPT masked edit redrew the whole scene at a different scale. Check carefully | — |

When unsure, **run 2–3 models in parallel on the same prompt** (5 parallel image jobs worked without throttling)
and pick the best. It costs well under $0.50 and saves rounds of iteration.

## Calling the gateway
Needs `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` in the env (never print it). Node ≥ 22 for AI SDK 7.
`npm i ai @ai-sdk/gateway undici`. Wrapping these calls in small `gen-image.mjs` / `gen-video.mjs` CLI helpers that write a sidecar `.json` with the billed cost pays off quickly.
```bash
G=<path>/gen-image.mjs
$G --model openai/gpt-image-2.5-sunburst --aspect 3:5 --long 1600 --ref source_2x.png --ref ref_species.jpg --prompt "$(cat prompt.txt)" --out out/sunburst-1.png
$G --model google/gemini-3-pro-image --image-size 2K --aspect 2:3 --ref source_2x.png --prompt "$P" --out out/nbpro-1.png
$G --model bytedance/seedream-5.0-pro --size 1248x2080 --ref source_2x.png --prompt "$P" --out out/seedream-1.jpg
# prints {"files":[...],"model":...,"seconds":..,"cost":..}
```
Minimal code (what the helpers do):
```js
import { generateImage, generateText } from 'ai';
import { createGateway } from '@ai-sdk/gateway';
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
const gateway = createGateway();                      // reads AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY
const src = readFileSync('source_2x.png');
// A) OpenAI / Flux / Seedream: generateImage with prompt {text, images}
const r = await generateImage({ model: gateway.imageModel('openai/gpt-image-2.5-sunburst'),
  prompt: { text: PROMPT, images: [src] }, size: '960x1600',
  providerOptions: { openai: { quality: 'high' } } });  // gateway default is LOW quality
writeFileSync('out.png', r.images[0].uint8Array);
// Seedream: needs size WxH (ignores aspectRatio) + providerOptions.bytedance.watermark=false
// B) Nano Banana (Gemini image) = chat model: generateText + file part, read result.files
const g = await generateText({ model: gateway('google/gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview'),
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: [{ type: 'text', text: PROMPT }, { type: 'file', data: src, mediaType: 'image/png' }] }],
  providerOptions: { google: { responseModalities: ['TEXT','IMAGE'], imageConfig: { aspectRatio: '2:3' } } } });
const img = g.files.find(f => f.mediaType?.startsWith('image/')); writeFileSync('out.png', img.uint8Array);
```
- Node's built-in fetch rejects an npm-`undici` Agent. For long calls, pass `fetch: (u,i)=>undiciFetch(u,{...i,dispatcher:agent})`
  to `createGateway` (20 min header and body timeouts).
- GPT Image 2.x takes flexible sizes (multiples of 16). gpt-image-1/1.5 take only 1024², 1536×1024 and 1024×1536.
- List what this key can use right now: `GET https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/models` (filter `type` image/video).

## Prompt pattern (worked for a person-into-fish transformation)
1. **Name the input**: "Edit the FIRST image (a selfie of a woman)."
2. **Keep list, exhaustive**: same face shape, eyes, glasses, hair color and length, earrings, blouse, room objects,
   lighting, **framing**.
3. **Change list, specific and physical**: what appears where ("mottled olive/brown skin spreading from collar to jaw
   and one cheek; fanned pectoral fin from the shoulder; spiny dorsal ridge out of the hair; red gill slits on the neck").
4. **Reference image for the species or object** as the SECOND image, labeled in the prompt. Download real photos first
   (Wikimedia) so a species reads correctly. Describe its signature traits in words too.
5. **Expression** spelled out ("eyes wide, eyebrows raised high, jaw dropped in a gasp, looking at the camera").
6. Style lock + "Do not add any text."

Retouch prompt (flattering, when asked): "Subtle beauty retouch of this exact photo. Keep her clearly the SAME person…
Change ONLY facial and neck skin: smoother, softened fine lines… a few years younger. Natural texture, not plastic. Keep
everything else exactly (including any fins, gills, teeth)." Run it on both the start and end frames when they feed a video.

## Workflow tips
- Upscale tiny sources 2x LANCZOS first (`source_2x.png`). Edits come back sharper.
- Save prompts as files (`prompt1.txt`, `rprompt.txt`) and runs as `run_*.sh` so a re-run is one command.
- Output aspect: request the source's aspect (3:5 or 2:3 for phone selfies) or the model may pad or reframe.
- After generation, resize to 1080 wide and caption with `meme-captioning-pil`. Deliver both clean and captioned versions.
- 2-panel "before → after" (real source on top, AI result below) often lands better than the result alone.

## Failure modes
| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| Different person / different room | Switch to Sunburst. Lengthen the keep list. Drop Flux Kontext |
| Zoomed out or reframed | Common with NB Pro. Crop back to the source framing, or use Sunburst |
| Empty `files` from Gemini | Use the `-preview` model id, then fall back to GA. Log `finishReason` |
| Looks washed out or low detail | GPT quality defaulted to low. Pass `quality: 'high'` |
| "AI generated" stamp | Seedream: `watermark:false` |
| Many failed edit attempts on a cartoon | Stop. Look again for a real frame plus overlays/captions (that's what shipped) |

skills.name: meme-video-editing
skills.description: Use when making a video meme from real footage. Covers grabbing clips, cutting and reordering segments cleanly, matching loudness, burning in subtitles or meme captions, tracking logos and labels onto faces, freeze frames, silent versions, and frame-by-frame verification.
skills.content:
---
name: meme-video-editing
description: >-
  Use when making a video meme from real footage. Covers grabbing clips, cutting
  and reordering segments cleanly, matching loudness, burning in subtitles or
  meme captions, tracking logos and labels onto faces, freeze frames, silent
  versions, and frame-by-frame verification.
---
# Video memes from real footage

**Real footage with text on it beats everything else.** A Ken Burns zoom/pan over real still panels was rejected as
"just an animated slide show". The same joke as captions over the actual episode clip was a hit. Only reach for
AI video (`meme-ai-video-generation`) when you need motion that doesn't exist.

## Pipeline overview
1. `yt-dlp` the source clips into `raw/` (plus auto-subs `.vtt` for rough line timing). See `meme-template-sourcing`.
2. Find exact cut points with Whisper word timestamps and the waveform.
3. `build_base_vN.py`: cut segments to a uniform format and concat with per-clip gain → `clips/base_vN.mov`.
4. `subs_vN.py`: write the ASS (and SRT) from a Python list.
5. `render_vN.py`: decode frames → composite overlays in PIL → encode with subtitles, loudnorm and a freeze tail.
6. Extract stills at every shot start and end, view them, then deliver. Also make a `-silent` version.
Bump N for every revision and keep the old scripts. A re-render takes about a minute.

## 2. Clean cut points (no clipped words)
```python
from faster_whisper import WhisperModel                 # small.en on CPU int8 is fine
m=WhisperModel("small.en",device="cpu",compute_type="int8")
segs,_=m.transcribe("clip.wav",word_timestamps=True,vad_filter=False,beam_size=5)
for s in segs: print(" ".join(f"{w.word.strip()}@{w.start:.2f}-{w.end:.2f}" for w in s.words))
```
Cut in the gap between words (≥40 ms after the last word end). Then confirm on a waveform plot
(`matplotlib`, RMS dB envelope at 20 ms) that no syllable is chopped. Listen-check by extracting the
boundary ±1 s to wav.

## 3. Segment cutting and concat (exact frame counts, uniform frame, micro-fades)
```python
SEGS=[("s0_setup","SRC_A",10.00,23.00),("s1_reply","SRC_B",0.15,3.60)]   # name, raw id, start, end (s)
VF={"SRC_B":"crop=1232:596:26:62,scale=1280:620:flags=lanczos","SRC_A":"crop=1280:620:0:51"}  # per-source crop to the same picture
for name,src,a,b in SEGS:
    N=round((b-a)*30); D=N/30
    vf=f"fps=30,{VF[src]},pad=1280:720:0:50:black,setsar=1,format=yuv420p"
    af=f"aresample=48000,aformat=channel_layouts=stereo,atrim=duration={D},afade=t=in:d=0.03,areverse,afade=t=in:d=0.03,areverse"
    subprocess.run(["ffmpeg","-v","error","-y","-ss",str(a),"-t",str(D+0.5),"-i",f"raw/{src}.mp4","-vf",vf,"-frames:v",str(N),
        "-af",af,"-c:v","libx264","-crf","12","-preset","fast","-c:a","pcm_s16le",f"clips/{name}.mov"],check=True)
```
- The 30 ms fade in and out on each segment (fade → `areverse` → fade → `areverse`) removes clicks at cuts.
- Save a `segments_vN.json` with `out_f0` (first output frame) per segment. Overlays are keyed by frame index.
  When you **reorder** shots, write a mapping function (`def v3(i): return i+390 if i<728 else i+378`) instead of redoing tracking.
- Setup scene first, payoff montage second. Reordering is cheap with this structure.

**Loudness matching**: measure each segment and gain-correct in the concat (one clip measured −27.4 LUFS, another −16.4,
an 11 dB jump):
```bash
ffmpeg -hide_banner -nostats -i clips/s0_setup.mov -af ebur128 -f null - 2>&1 | grep "I:" | tail -1
```
```python
GAIN={"s0_setup":5.0,"s1_reply":-4.5}   # dB, bring each to ≈ -22 LUFS
fc="".join(f"[{k}:a]volume={GAIN[m]}dB[a{k}];" for k,m in enumerate(names))+"".join(f"[{k}:v][a{k}]" for k in range(len(names)))
fc+=f"concat=n={len(names)}:v=1:a=1[v][a]"
```

## 4. Burned-in subtitles (movie style, ASS)
```python
SUBS=[(0.15,1.45,"First subtitle."),(2.20,4.20,"First line\\Nsecond line"),
      (38.55,40.00,"{\\i1}Voice on the phone{\\i0}")]          # ≤2 lines, timed to the actual speech
def ts(t): return f"{int(t//3600)}:{int(t%3600//60):02d}:{t%60:05.2f}"
hdr="""[Script Info]
ScriptType: v4.00+
PlayResX: 1280
PlayResY: 720
WrapStyle: 2
ScaledBorderAndShadow: yes

[V4+ Styles]
Format: Name, Fontname, Fontsize, PrimaryColour, SecondaryColour, OutlineColour, BackColour, Bold, Italic, Underline, StrikeOut, ScaleX, ScaleY, Spacing, Angle, BorderStyle, Outline, Shadow, Alignment, MarginL, MarginR, MarginV, Encoding
Style: Movie,Arimo,46,&H00FFFFFF,&H00FFFFFF,&H00000000,&H96000000,-1,0,0,0,100,100,0,0,1,3.2,1.2,2,60,60,26,1

[Events]
Format: Layer, Start, End, Style, Name, MarginL, MarginR, MarginV, Effect, Text
"""
open("subs.ass","w").write(hdr+"".join(f"Dialogue: 0,{ts(a)},{ts(b)},Movie,,0,0,0,,{t}\n" for a,b,t in SUBS))
```
Also write an `.srt` (replace `\N` with newlines, `{\i1}` with `<i>`) for platforms that want separate subs.
For **parody subs**, keep the original line structure and only swap words so the subtitle length matches the mouth movement.

Meme-style captions on a clip (Impact-like, centered, timed) with `drawtext`. Use `textfile=` to avoid escaping:
```python
f"drawtext=fontfile={FONT}:textfile={tf}:fontsize=46:fontcolor=white:borderw=4:bordercolor=black:"
f"x=(w-text_w)/2:y=h-text_h-28:enable='between(t\\,{t0}\\,{t1})'"     # prepend 'crop=iw:ih-28:0:0' to cut a watermark strip
```

## 5. Overlays on faces (logos or labels that follow people)
Detect faces per frame (OpenCV Haar: `haarcascade_frontalface_default` then `alt2` as fallback, `minSize=(120,120)`,
`equalizeHist` first) → `faces.json`. Make **grid sheets** (frames with 100 px gridlines plus detection boxes) to read
coordinates for manual keyframes where detection misses (back of a head, profile).

**Key lesson:** v1 sized each logo from the per-frame face width, so logos zoomed and pulsed with every detector jitter.
Fix: **constant size per shot, position only**. Fixed (median) if the head barely moves, otherwise heavily smoothed:
```python
def gsmooth(arr,sigma):
    r=int(3*sigma); k=np.exp(-0.5*(np.arange(-r,r+1)/sigma)**2); k/=k.sum()
    pad=np.pad(arr,((r,r),(0,0)),mode='edge'); return np.stack([np.convolve(pad[:,c],k,mode='valid') for c in range(arr.shape[1])],1)
def shot(a,b,filt,size,manual=(),still_thresh=70,sigma=12):
    """Constant icon size for the whole shot. Position = median if head barely moves, else heavily smoothed path."""
    keys={}
    for i in range(a,b+1):
        for (x,y,w,h) in faces.get(i,[]):
            cx,cy=x+w/2,y+h/2
            if filt(cx,cy,w): keys[i]=(cx,cy); break
    for (i,cx,cy) in manual: keys[i]=(cx,cy)                 # manual keyframes for missed detections
    ks=sorted(keys); P=np.array([keys[k] for k in ks],float)
    if np.ptp(P[:,0])<still_thresh and np.ptp(P[:,1])<still_thresh:
        c=np.median(P,0); return {i:(c[0],c[1],size) for i in range(a,b+1)}, 'fixed'
    xs=np.interp(range(a,b+1),ks,P[:,0]); ys=np.interp(range(a,b+1),ks,P[:,1])
    path=gsmooth(np.stack([xs,ys],1),sigma)
    return {i:(path[i-a,0],path[i-a,1],size) for i in range(a,b+1)}, 'glide'
```
- Filter detections per shot by plausible box size and region (`lambda cx,cy,w: 130<=w<=260 and 600<=cx<=950`).
- Fade alpha out when the person walks out of frame. Clip pastes at the frame edges.
- Use **static** logos (no animation). They read as labels, not effects.
- **Staggered icon row** (e.g. when someone says "I have four of them"): fixed size, each icon starts 5 frames after
  the previous one and fades in over 5 frames: `al=min(1,(i-F0-5*j)/5)`.

Frame loop (decode → PIL → encode, with subtitles, loudnorm, freeze tail and audio fade in the same pass):
```python
dec=subprocess.Popen(["ffmpeg","-v","error","-i",BASE,"-f","rawvideo","-pix_fmt","rgba","-"],stdout=subprocess.PIPE)
enc=subprocess.Popen(["ffmpeg","-v","error","-y","-f","rawvideo","-pix_fmt","rgba","-s","1280x720","-r","30","-i","-","-i",BASE,
 "-filter_complex",f"[0:v]tpad=stop_mode=clone:stop_duration=1.0,subtitles={ASS}:fontsdir=/usr/share/fonts/truetype,format=yuv420p[v];"
 f"[1:a]loudnorm=I=-16:TP=-1.5:LRA=11,aresample=48000,afade=t=out:st={NF/30-0.12}:d=0.12,apad=pad_dur=1.0[a]",
 "-map","[v]","-map","[a]","-c:v","libx264","-preset","slow","-crf","18","-pix_fmt","yuv420p","-c:a","aac","-b:a","192k",
 "-movflags","+faststart","-shortest",OUT],stdin=subprocess.PIPE)
while (buf:=dec.stdout.read(W*H*4)) and len(buf)==W*H*4:
    fr=Image.frombuffer('RGBA',(W,H),buf,'raw','RGBA',0,1).copy(); draw_overlays(fr,i); enc.stdin.write(fr.tobytes()); i+=1
enc.stdin.close(); enc.wait()
```
`tpad … stop_duration=1.0` + `apad` = a **1 s freeze on the last beat**. Lets the punchline land.

## 6. Variants and verification
```bash
ffmpeg -v error -y -i out.mp4 -an -c:v copy out-silent.mp4                      # silent version (autoplay feeds)
for t in 0.2 13.1 16.5 24.7 34.3 37.3 45.5; do ffmpeg -v error -y -ss $t -i out.mp4 -frames:v 1 -q:v 3 stills/v4_${t}s.jpg; done
ffprobe -v error -show_entries stream=codec_type,width,height,r_frame_rate:format=duration -of compact=p=0 out.mp4
```
- [ ] Stills at each shot's first and last frames: overlay on the right person, constant size, nothing off-frame
- [ ] Subtitles ≤2 lines, not covering overlays, appear with the speech (not before)
- [ ] No clipped words at cuts. Even loudness across shots (re-run ebur128 on the output)
- [ ] Freeze tail present. Duration as expected. Audio stream present (or absent for `-silent`)

skills.name: meme-ai-video-generation
skills.description: Use when a meme needs motion that doesn't exist in real footage, such as animating a transformation between two stills or bringing a photo to life. Covers model choice (Kling 3.0 I2V with start and end frames first), gateway calls, prompts, costs, and checking the output.
skills.content:
---
name: meme-ai-video-generation
description: >-
  Use when a meme needs motion that doesn't exist in real footage, such as
  animating a transformation between two stills or bringing a photo to life.
  Covers model choice (Kling 3.0 I2V with start and end frames first), gateway
  calls, prompts, costs, and checking the output.
---
# AI image-to-video for memes

Use only when real footage can't do it (see `meme-video-editing`). Always drive it from **real or approved stills**
(image-to-video), never text-to-video recreations of known characters (they come out off-model).

## Model choice (from a real portrait transformation clip: start frame = real selfie, end frame = AI-transformed still)
| Model id | Result | Output | Cost / time (6 s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `klingai/kling-v3.0-i2v` with `--image START --end-image END` | **Best fit.** Kept portrait framing and identity, hit the end frame | 744×1236, 24 fps, silent | **≈$1.01**, 55–125 s |
| `minimax/minimax-h3-max` | Good backup, fast and cheap. Has an audio track | 768×1280, 24 fps (+ audio stream) | $0.48, ~24 s |
| `alibaba/wan-v3.0-video` | ❌ for portrait: came back **1280×720 landscape** and outpainted the sides | 1280×720, 30 fps | $0.60, ~110 s |
| `google/gemini-omni-flash-preview` | Chat model that emits video (use `generateText`). Has audio. Not tested on memes | 1280×720 | ≈$0.26 / 5 s |
| `spacexai/grok-imagine-video-1.5-lite` | Cheap draft or preview | 848×480 | $0.10 / 5 s |
| `bytedance/seedance-2.5` | Up to 30 s and many refs. Rejects an explicit ratio in I2V | 1280×720 | ≈$1.17 / 5 s |
Rule of thumb: Kling for the final, MiniMax as a cheap parallel backup. Run both at once (4 parallel video jobs worked).

## Prep the frames
- START = the real image (upscaled, cropped to the final aspect). END = the edited still from `meme-ai-image-editing`
  at the **same size and framing** (both 960×1600 here). Mismatched framing makes the model zoom or morph the camera.
- If the subject should look flattering or younger, **retouch both start and end** frames first (same retouch prompt on
  each), then generate the video from the retouched pair.

## Call it
```bash
G=<path>/gen-video.mjs     # small CLI helper if you have one; otherwise use the code below
$G --model klingai/kling-v3.0-i2v --duration 6 --image vid_start.jpg --end-image vid_end.jpg --prompt "$(cat vprompt.txt)" --out vid/kling.mp4
$G --model minimax/minimax-h3-max --duration 6 --image vid_start.jpg --end-image vid_end.jpg --prompt "$(cat vprompt.txt)" --out vid/minimax.mp4
```
```js
import { experimental_generateVideo as generateVideo } from 'ai';
import { createGateway } from '@ai-sdk/gateway';
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
const gateway = createGateway();   // AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY; use an undici Agent with 20-min timeouts for sync calls
const r = await generateVideo({ model: gateway.videoModel('klingai/kling-v3.0-i2v'), prompt: PROMPT, duration: 6,
  frameImages: [{ image: readFileSync('vid_start.jpg'), frameType: 'first_frame' },
                { image: readFileSync('vid_end.jpg'),   frameType: 'last_frame' }],
  generateAudio: false, maxRetries: 1, abortSignal: AbortSignal.timeout(900_000) });
writeFileSync('kling.mp4', r.videos[0].uint8Array);
```
Gateway quirks (all observed):
- **Local image bytes need one long synchronous request.** The async poll API caps the start request at 300 KiB, and even
  a 140 KB JPEG got `413 … Use hosted URLs`. With inline files, don't set `poll`. Use a long abort timeout instead.
- With a start frame, **don't send `aspectRatio`**. Most models take it from the image. Seedance rejects it, and Grok stretches the image.
- MiniMax ignores `generateAudio` and WxH resolutions (only 480P/768P). Drop `resolution` for it.
- Hosted result URLs expire in about 24 h. Download right away. The billed cost is in `providerMetadata.gateway.cost`,
  or call `gateway.getGenerationInfo({id})` for async jobs.
- Kling and Veo use no special tokens in prompts. Seedance uses `[Image 1]`, and Wan uses `character1`.

## Prompt pattern (one paragraph, chronological)
"<Who> takes a selfie in <place>, smiling. Then <transformation step by step, physical details>… Her smile switches straight
into wide-eyed shock: eyebrows shoot UP, eyes go wide… **No frowning, no furrowed brow, no squinting, no grimace.** Her face
stays smooth, soft and youthful the whole time, **the same person throughout**. Handheld phone selfie, realistic, same room,
same lighting, comedic transformation."
- The first Kling pass made the subject frown and squint (reads as older or wrinkled). The negative expression list fixed it.
- Repeat identity locks ("same person throughout", "same room, same lighting").

## Caption the clip
Render the caption once as a transparent PNG the size of the video, then overlay it (keeps the meme font and stroke identical to the stills):
```bash
python3 caption.py overlay 744 1236 cap.png      # PIL: transparent RGBA + top caption (see meme-captioning-pil)
ffmpeg -v error -y -i kling.mp4 -i cap.png -filter_complex "[0:v][1:v]overlay=0:0,format=yuv420p" -c:v libx264 -crf 18 -movflags +faststart out-captioned.mp4
```

## Verify
```bash
ffprobe -v error -show_entries stream=codec_type,width,height,r_frame_rate:format=duration -of compact=p=0 kling.mp4
for t in 0 1.5 3 4.5 5.9; do ffmpeg -v error -y -ss $t -i kling.mp4 -frames:v 1 -q:v 3 chk_$t.jpg; done
```
- [ ] Orientation and size match the stills (portrait stays portrait). No outpainted borders
- [ ] Same person in every sampled frame. No frowning or aging mid-clip. The end frame matches the edited still
- [ ] Audio: Kling and Wan are silent, MiniMax has a track. Strip it or replace it as needed (`-an`)
- [ ] Log model, prompt and cost (from the sidecar `.json`) in the request folder

skills.content:
---
name: meme-voice-dubbing
description: >-
  Use when a video meme needs characters to say new words in audio (parody
  dubs), not just new subtitles. Covers TTS through the Vercel AI Gateway, stem
  separation, word-level splicing, take selection by speaker similarity,
  matching timing, EQ and loudness, room tone, QA, and honest limits on voice
  likeness.
---
# Voice dubbing for video memes

Try subtitles first (`meme-video-editing`). They're cheaper and always clean. Dub when the user wants to *hear* it.
Expect "funny-bad," not seamless. Set that expectation up front.

## What the gateway offers (speech models, Oct 2026)
| Model | Voices | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `fish-audio/s2.1-pro` (also s2-pro, s1) | Any **Fish library voice id** (32-hex) as `voice` | Large community library to cast from. Returns mp3 |
| `google/gemini-3.8-flash-tts` (+ `-lite`) | Named voices (Sadaltager, Iapetus, Umbriel, Charon, Orus, Schedar, Rasalgethi, Aoede…) | Takes `instructions` for delivery ("smooth, smug drawl of a middle-aged corporate boss") |
| `openai/tts-1-hd`, `openai/tts-1` | Stock voices | Clean, generic |
| `spacexai/grok-tts`, `microsoft/mai-voice-2.1(-flash)` | Stock voices | — |
**No reference-clip voice cloning through the gateway.** You can only *cast* the closest stock or library voice.

```js
import { experimental_generateSpeech as generateSpeech } from 'ai';
import { gateway } from '@ai-sdk/gateway';
const args = { model: gateway.speechModel(job.model), text: job.text };
if (job.voice) args.voice = job.voice; if (job.instructions) args.instructions = job.instructions;
if (!job.model.startsWith('fish')) args.outputFormat = 'wav';          // fish returns mp3
const r = await generateSpeech(args); await writeFile(job.out, r.audio.uint8Array);
```
Batch it: a `jobs.json` list of `{model, voice, out, text, instructions}` run by 6 parallel workers (the failures are logged and the rest carry on).

## Pipeline
1. **Separate dialogue from music and effects**: `demucs -n htdemucs --two-stems=vocals -o work/sep work/clip_stereo.wav`
   → `work/sep/htdemucs/clip_stereo/{vocals,no_vocals}.wav` (no_vocals is the bed).
2. **Reference voices per character**: cut 3–8 clean spans of each actor from the vocal stem (16 kHz mono), in `ref/<spk>_N.wav`.
3. **Cast voices**: generate the same sample line with 5–10 candidate voices × 2 takes each, score with ECAPA (below), and pick the
   top per character. Pitch-match diagnostics: median F0 via `librosa.pyin`. Report the needed semitone shift.
4. **Line table** (one row per changed span):
   `(id, speaker, tts_text_with_context, words_to_extract|None, window=(t0,t1) to place, region=(t0,t1) to mute, fx 'film'|'phone', instructions)`
   Generate the **whole sentence** for context and natural prosody, then cut out only the needed words.
5. **Takes**: 3–11 takes per line. For each: Whisper word timestamps → fuzzy-match the target words (`difflib` ratio ≥ 0.7,
   numbers normalized "10"→"ten") → cut with 40/60 ms margins → trim edge silence.
6. **Pick the best take**: `cost = |ln(dur/window)| − 0.5·ecapa_sim + (3 if transcript_acc<0.97 else 0)`.
7. **Fit**: rubberband time-stretch with formants preserved, clamped to 0.85–1.45 (0.7–2.0 for <0.4 s windows), optional ±1 semitone:
   `ffmpeg -i in.wav -af "rubberband=tempo=1.08:pitch=1.0:formant=preserved:pitchq=quality:window=short" out.wav`
8. **Match the room**: EQ-match the long-term spectrum to that actor's original stem (Welch LTAS diff, 1/3-octave smoothing,
   clipped ±10 dB, FIR via `firwin2`) → light compression (`acompressor=threshold=0.08:ratio=4:attack=3:release=60`) → 12 ms
   fades → scale to the **active RMS** of the original voice in that region → peak-limit to 1.6× the original peak.
   Phone voices: band-pass 320–3300 Hz + soft `tanh` saturation.
9. **Mix** (two styles):
   - **Snippet splice**: `new = mix − vocals·mask + dub + room_tone`. Only changed words are swapped (mask with 15 ms ramps).
     Keeps the real actors everywhere else. The swaps are **audibly jarring** (which can be the joke).
   - **Full re-voice**: `new = no_vocals_bed + dub_stem + room_tone`. Every line is TTS. Consistent, but clearly not the cast.
10. **Room tone**: shaped noise from the quietest 15% of 20 ms frames of the vocal stem around each region (Welch PSD → FIR),
    RMS-matched, faded 30 ms, so muted gaps don't go dead silent.
11. **Peak control**: if any region peak exceeds 0.95, trim only the dub stem there and repeat up to 6 times.
12. **Mux**: `ffmpeg -i video.mp4 -i work/dub_mix.wav -map 0:v -map 1:a -c:v copy -c:a aac -b:a 192k -shortest out-dub.mp4`

### ECAPA speaker similarity
```python
from speechbrain.inference.speaker import EncoderClassifier
enc=EncoderClassifier.from_hparams(source='speechbrain/spkrec-ecapa-voxceleb',savedir='~/.cache/sb_ecapa',run_opts={'device':'cpu'})
def emb(x16k):                      # float32 mono 16 kHz; band-limit candidates 90-7000 Hz first
    e=enc.encode_batch(torch.from_numpy(x16k).unsqueeze(0)).squeeze().numpy(); return e/np.linalg.norm(e)
ref=np.mean([emb(load(p)) for p in ref_parts],0); ref/=np.linalg.norm(ref); sim=float(emb(take)@ref)
```

## QA (run every time; `check_dub.py` pattern)
- **Unchanged regions identical**: diff original vs dub outside the regions. It should be AAC re-encode noise only.
- Per-line table: mix dB, voice dB (orig vs dub), and the **edge jump** at region boundaries (dub jump minus original jump).
- Spectral balance per band (80–250 … 4k–8k Hz) of the dub stem vs the original speaker, normalized at 500–2 kHz.
- **Whisper transcript of the final mix**. Read it. Product and brand names get mangled (a two-word product name came back as one nonsense word) and plurals drop
  ("ten minutes" heard as "ten minute"). Normalize in matching (a `{"10":"ten","ten-minute":"ten"}`-style map). Regenerate those takes with spelled-out text.
- Waveform/RMS plot of original vs dub with the regions shaded (`matplotlib`, saved to `work/waveform_compare.png`).

## Honest limits (measured)
| Comparison | ECAPA cosine |
|---|---|
| Same actor, different clips | 0.48–0.96 (typically 0.6–0.9) |
| Two *different* real actors | 0.25–0.31 |
| Best cast TTS take vs the target actor | 0.30–0.39; many short words 0.05–0.2 |
Stock TTS sounds about as much like the actor as *a different person* does. Tell the user that.

## Real cloning (not via the gateway; ask first)
Fish Audio's own API (custom voice from reference audio) or ElevenLabs Instant Voice Cloning would get much closer. They need a
direct account and payment, and **consent and ToS compliance**: cloning a real actor's voice usually breaks provider terms, so stick to
voices you have rights to, and label parodies as parody.

## Failure modes
| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| A word is cut off or the take includes the next word | Widen the margins. Bound the cut by the neighboring word's start and end |
| Tempo artifacts (chipmunk or slurry) | Generate more takes and pick by duration fit before stretching more than 1.45× |
| Dub too loud or bright vs the scene | EQ match + active-RMS match. Check the edge-jump column |
| Gaps sound dead | Add room tone under the mask |
| Clipping after mixing | Region peak-trim loop on the dub stem only |

---
name: meme-delivery-and-library
description: >-
  Use when a meme or meme video is finished and must be shown to the user,
  handed to another agent, emailed, uploaded to the user's cloud library folder,
  or logged. Also use when setting up or maintaining the local template and meme
  library.
---
# Delivering and filing memes

A meme isn't done until the user can see it, the files are named and versioned, and the log is updated.

## Pick the delivery channel
| Destination | How | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| The chat with the user (image) | Attach the image itself through the chat tool's image or attachment field (e.g. SendToUser `images` with the `file://` path) | Show the image, not just a path. Send the JPG (not a multi-MB PNG) |
| The chat (video / large file) | Send as an attachment | Also include a still or contact sheet so it previews at a glance |
| Another agent that requested it | SendToAgent with `images: [{"url":"file:///abs/path.jpg"}]` (priority if time-sensitive) + a one-line note | The requester posts it. Don't message humans directly unless told to |
| Email | Gmail `create_draft` (reply: pass `replyToMessageId`) → **UploadFile** to that `draftId` → user approves → `send_message` with the draftId | Attach **last**: `update_draft` drops attachments. Keep under 25 MB. Sending needs explicit approval |
| The user's cloud library folder (e.g. Drive) | **UploadFile** with `destination.folderId` (or `path`) | Use the folder ids the user gave you. One file per call |
| Their computer | CopyFromBox | — |

Anything visible to other people (sending email, posting, sharing a link) needs the user's explicit OK for that specific action.

## Upload pitfalls (observed)
- **Don't push binaries through a connector's `create_file` text/base64 field.** JPEG payloads above roughly 2.5k base64
  chars arrived corrupted. Many attempts went into size probes, chunked base64 and payload compaction before giving up. Use UploadFile
  (bytes go straight from your computer). If that's unavailable, upload through the browser's normal web UI.
- After uploading, check that the result (name, link, mimeType) is real, and open the link or thumbnail if you can.
- Don't leave scratch files (`*.b64`, probe jpgs, payload json) in the library root. Use `$MEMES/scratch/`.

## Library layout
```
$MEMES/
  templates/<slug>/        blank.jpg, blank-hires.jpg, with-quote.jpg, TEMPLATE.md, meta.json
  templates/<pool>/        themed pools for recurring series (e.g. motivation/<who>-<scene>-blank.jpg)
  candidates/<series>/     unused frames found while sourcing + USED.md
  requests/<slug>/         per-request working dir: prompts, raw model outputs + sidecar json, build script vN
  finished/                <slug>-vN.jpg (and -clean / -2panel variants); recurring: <series>-YYYY-MM-DD-<day>-<time>.jpg
  video/<project>/         clips/, work/, logos/, build script, outputs <project>-vN.mp4 (+ -silent, -dub)
  scripts/                 reusable makers (caption, badges, overlays)
  scratch/
```
- **Never overwrite a delivered version.** Bump `-vN`, so "go back to v3" is always possible.
- Keep the build script beside the output so a tweak is one edit plus a rerun.

### meta.json (per template)
```json
{"name":"We Don't Do That Here","slug":"we-dont-do-that-here","type":"reaction still + fixed quote",
 "character":"T'Challa (Chadwick Boseman)","source_film":"Avengers: Infinity War (2018)",
 "canonical_line":"We don't do that here","usage":"Top: the faux pas. Punchline: the still + line.",
 "files":{"blank":"…-blank.jpg","blank_hires":"…-blank-hires.jpg","with_quote":"…-with-quote.jpg"},
 "sources":{"know_your_meme":"https://knowyourmeme.com/…","imgflip":"https://imgflip.com/meme/…"},"saved":"YYYY-MM-DD"}
```
TEMPLATE.md holds the same facts in prose plus caption-zone notes (see `meme-template-sourcing`). Upload the TEMPLATE.md
next to the blank in the cloud "source images" folder, so the library is usable from anywhere.

## Log every meme (the user's log page or database, plus a local line)
One row per delivered meme or version:
| Field | Example |
|---|---|
| Date (user's TZ) | 2026-09-12 |
| Request / joke | "my bank account after connecting it to the assistant" |
| Template + source | You Live Like This, imgflip id / episode + frame time |
| Tools / models + cost | Pillow + Liberation Sans Bold; Sunburst edit $0.05 |
| Files | finished/<slug>-v5.jpg + cloud link |
| Feedback | "drop the bottom caption" → v5 |
Also keep a **Learnings** list (what failed and the fix) and a **Software trials** table (tool, date, verdict, cost).
If the log lives in a tool you were told to keep read-only, write the log locally and hand the text to the parent or user.

## Verify before saying "done"
- [ ] The user saw the image or got the attachment (video), plus a 1–2 line note on the joke and template source
- [ ] Final file is in `finished/` with a versioned name. The build script is saved
- [ ] Uploaded copy opens (not corrupted, right size). Link captured in the log
- [ ] Template blank + TEMPLATE.md + meta.json saved if the template is new
- [ ] Log row added. Any new lesson added to Learnings
- [ ] No outbound message, email or share happened without explicit approval
